intent_en: To demonstrate that the income distribution in the depicted context is high, allowing for luxury housing at the average level and ensuring even the lowest earners are wealthier than the average American.
previous_intent: To illustrate the high income levels in high-cost areas like San Francisco, demonstrating that the average standard of living is substantial and even the lowest earners in this group exceed the national average income.
narration_support: Average, meaning many can afford a big fancy house, or rent a closet in San Francisco. Even the lowest paid 10 % make more than the average American.
chart_support: Bell curve distribution showing the bottom segment shaded below the average (AVG) line, with a luxury house icon positioned at the higher end of the distribution.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly claims the lowest earners exceed the American average and mentions luxury housing. The chart visualizes a distribution with a bottom tail below the average and a house icon indicating high value on the right.
